entries.title: A receiver call a.b(..) is no longer also reported as a bare call b(..) (#43)
entries.summary: The lexical call scanner matched a.b( as a receiver call, then read b again as the next word and reported it a second time without a receiver.
highlights: A receiver call a.b(..) is no longer also reported as a bare call b(..) (#43). The lexical call scanner matched a.b( as a receiver call, then read b again as the next word and reported it a second time without a receiver. That copy went through the bare-name fallback, which binds a callee name declared exactly once in the repository whatever the receiver's type, so Canvas.render('x', 80) on an unindexed type became a caller of the repository's only Template.render — the external-type guard from #32 applies only to calls that carry their receiver. The scanner now skips the receiver path and the method name after a receiver call, and the receiver keeps its whole dotted path (StringUtils.INSTANCE.countWords(..) → receiver StringUtils.INSTANCE, so a Kotlin object called from Groovy still resolves); chained calls (a.b().c()) and calls nested in the arguments are still reported.

Groovy E2E Group K (test K1): a call on an unindexed type, on its own line and in a one-line method, is not a caller of the repository's unique same-named method, while a call through a receiver of the declaring type is. Parser unit test for plain, chained, nested, this. and dotted-path (StringUtils.INSTANCE.) receiver calls.
Re-index Groovy repositories with knot-indexer --clean to drop the false CALLS edges.

entries.title: Postman collection brought up to date
entries.summary: KNOT_SERVER_STUCK_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS (default 60, minimum 1): how often the server looks for repositories stuck in cloning / pulling / indexing with no worker holding their lock.
highlights: KNOT_SERVER_STUCK_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS (default 60, minimum 1): how often the server looks for repositories stuck in cloning / pulling / indexing with no worker holding their lock.

Postman collection brought up to date with the current API: correct registration bodies, a webhook request with its token header, the repo detail, entity graph (including ROUTES_TO), graph expand and metrics requests, and every MCP tool.

A repository could stay in cloning forever (#10). A second knot-server started on the same workspace and port loaded the registry, re-enqueued every unfinished repository, and its worker claimed one (and began wiping it) before the process failed to bind the port and exited. The running server then dropped its own job for that repository as stale, and nothing reset the status until the daily scheduler poll. Now the server binds its port before touching the registry (failed to bind …: is another knot-server already listening on it?); startup recovery skips repositories whose lock a live node holds, so restarting a cluster node no longer resets another node's in-flight job; a new check (KNOT_SERVER_STUCK_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECS, default 60s) re-enqueues a repository seen in cloning / pulling / indexing with no lock holder on two consecutive passes; the stale-lock recovery never removes a lock file that is still held; and a dropped job logs the status it found (repo no longer Queued (found: cloning)).

highlights: Upgrade knot to 1.12.1. Updated the knot dependency from 1.12.0 to 1.12.1. Upstream, a Groovy receiver call a.b(..) is no longer also reported as a bare call b(..), so a call on an unindexed type (Canvas.render(..)) no longer becomes a caller of the repository's only same-named method; the receiver keeps its whole dotted path (StringUtils.INSTANCE.countWords(..)). entries.title: HTTP endpoint catalogue (#33, phase 1)
highlights: HTTP endpoint catalogue (#33, phase 1). JAX-RS (class/method @Path + @GET/@POST/@PUT/@DELETE/@PATCH/@HEAD/@OPTIONS) and Spring MVC (class @RequestMapping + @GetMapping/@PostMapping/@PutMapping/@DeleteMapping/@PatchMapping or @RequestMapping(method = …)) handlers produce one http_endpoint entity per <METHOD> <path>, linked to the handler by a new ROUTES_TO edge. Class and method paths are joined and normalized, path arrays expand, path-variable patterns are dropped ({id: [0-9]+} → {id}), and a @RequestMapping without method is ANY. Paths built from string constants resolve: literals, + concatenation, Kotlin const val templates, constants of the same file (Java static final fields and interface constants, Kotlin top-level/object/companion const val) and constants declared in another file of the repository, located through the endpoint file's imports and package, then among the parsed files or by the <package>/<Type>.java|.kt layout (so an incremental run that re-parses only the controller still resolves them). Declarative clients (@FeignClient, @RegisterRestClient interfaces) are not endpoints. Paths are relative to the application: the context path is not applied.

list_endpoints MCP tool and knot endpoints CLI command (--method, --path, --repo, table/markdown/JSON). The path filter is a segment-wise prefix in which an endpoint's {variable} segment matches any value, so a concrete URL (/api/owners/42) finds its endpoint. find_callers gains an HTTP routes bucket (routes_to), so a handler reached only over HTTP is never reported as unused; explore_file groups endpoints under HTTP Endpoints; the subgraph query (used by knot-server's graph API) accepts ROUTES_TO. knot-server's /mcp endpoint serves the new tool through the shared tool list.

Class annotations are recorded when tree-sitter-kotlin-ng parses them as an expression before the declaration (@RestController\n@RequestMapping("/api")\nclass … with a body); previously the class had no decorators.

Java E2E tests 56–62 (fixture testing_files/java/http_endpoints/: JAX-RS resource with an interface constant from another file, Spring controller, Feign client) and Kotlin E2E tests 31–32 (fixture testing_files/kotlin/http_endpoints/). Unit tests for the annotation reader, constant evaluation, path normalization, each framework, client exclusion, cross-file constants (same batch and disk-only), the ROUTES_TO resolution, the endpoint filters and the Kotlin class annotations. Measured on spring-petclinic (17/17 endpoints), jhipster-sample-app (48/48), tut-spring-boot-kotlin (6/6) and quarkus-super-heroes (3/3; its REST clients excluded, its OpenAPI-generated interfaces are not in the source tree).

entries.title: Same-named Java/Kotlin types in different packages resolve through the caller's…
entries.summary: A call on a receiver typed Config bound to whichever Config had the lexicographically smallest FQN, and a type reference or extends to an ambiguous name produced no edge at all.
highlights: Same-named Java/Kotlin types in different packages resolve through the caller's imports and package (#45). A call on a receiver typed Config bound to whichever Config had the lexicographically smallest FQN, and a type reference or extends to an ambiguous name produced no edge at all. Java and Kotlin entities now carry their file's package and imports (ImportScope: single-type imports keyed by simple name or Kotlin as alias, and on-demand imports; static imports are left out). An unqualified, capitalized type name is pinned, in Java/Kotlin precedence order, to a single-type import, then a type of the caller's own package, then an on-demand import. A pinned type binds calls only within itself and its own supertypes (the extends map is now also keyed by FQN, so a pinned type never borrows the parents of a homonym), applies to receivers named after their type (Kotlin config.load() → Config), and resolves extends / type references to that exact FQN. A single-type import of a type no indexed repository declares leaves the call or reference unresolved instead of binding to a repository homonym. Files without imports (other languages) are unaffected.

Java E2E tests 51–55 (fixture testing_files/java/import_homonyms/): explicit, same-package and on-demand imports pick b.Config, an inherited method comes from the imported type's own supertype, an external import binds nothing, and extends follows the import. Kotlin E2E tests 27–28 now include a consumer in a third package that imports each Config, one through an as alias. Parser unit test for Java/Kotlin import scopes; resolver unit tests for each precedence rule, inherited methods, external imports and type references.
Re-index Java and Kotlin repositories with knot-indexer --clean.

entries.title: Calls inside one-line methods are attached to them (#40)
entries.summary: Lexical call references carry a line but no column, and a call was assigned to a method only when its line came strictly after the declaration line, so String wide(Formatter f) { f.format('x', 80) }…
highlights: Calls inside one-line methods are attached to them (#40). Lexical call references carry a line but no column, and a call was assigned to a method only when its line came strictly after the declaration line, so String wide(Formatter f) { f.format('x', 80) } had no outgoing CALLS edge and its callees looked unused. Turning the comparison inclusive would have reported the declaration as calls too: the method's own name and typed parameters such as Formatter f, which read like a command call. Declaration lines are now skipped and only the method body that opens on them (between its { and the matching }) is rescanned, so one-line methods, calls inside a one-line closure and calls after the { of a multi-line method's first line all reach their method. A call on the declaration line of a method nested in another one no longer falls back to the outer method either. Synthesized property accessors, which start on the property line, never take a closure-valued property's calls.

Groovy E2E Group J (tests J1–J4): one-line methods with receiver, bare and closure calls list their callers, and a declaration is never a call to the method itself. Parser unit tests for one-line methods, the first line of a multi-line method and closure-valued properties.
Re-index Groovy repositories with knot-indexer --clean to add the missing edges.

entries.title: Variables local to a function no longer become class members (#41)
entries.summary: The lexical_declaration query matched declarations at any depth, so const url = new URL(pageURL) inside CdpPage.deleteCookie was indexed as the constant CdpPage.url.
highlights: Variables local to a function no longer become class members (#41). The lexical_declaration query matched declarations at any depth, so const url = new URL(pageURL) inside CdpPage.deleteCookie was indexed as the constant CdpPage.url. It captured this.url() calls meant for the inherited Page.url(), shared the FQN Page.url with the real method, appeared as a member in explore_file and search, and duplicated its initializer's CALLS edges. A JS/TS const / let / var declared inside a function, method or arrow body is no longer indexed; its initializer's calls stay on the enclosing entity. Module-level constants, class fields and local function definitions are unchanged.

An explicit this.m() / self.m() walks the enclosing type's supertypes breadth-first, nearest first, as static receivers already did. Previously only Python's self looked at direct parents, so in TypeScript, Java or Kotlin this.url() on an inherited method stayed unresolved, or fell back to a same-named method elsewhere, whenever several classes declared url.

TypeScript E2E tests 17–19 (fixture testing_files/typescript/this_inherited/): this.url() in CdpPage extends Page binds to Page.url despite a local const url and an unrelated Frame.url, and explore_file lists no local constant. Extractor unit tests for TS and JS locals (methods, functions, arrows, callbacks); resolver unit test for this calls through two supertype levels.
Re-index TypeScript/JavaScript repositories with knot-indexer --clean to drop the local-variable entities and their edges.

entries.title: HTTP endpoints in the graph API and viewer
entries.summary: The graph API accepts ROUTES_TO in relationships and a new endpoints kind category (http_endpoint), so relationships=ROUTES_TO&kinds=endpoints,functions returns the endpoint → handler map without the…
highlights: HTTP endpoints in the graph API and viewer. The graph API accepts ROUTES_TO in relationships and a new endpoints kind category (http_endpoint), so relationships=ROUTES_TO&kinds=endpoints,functions returns the endpoint → handler map without the noisy other category (which turns the kind filter off). The /graph viewer gains a Routes relationship toggle and an Endpoints kind toggle; turning on Routes turns on Endpoints and Functions.

list_endpoints MCP tool and routes_to callers bucket. Served through knot's shared tool list and callers output: /mcp lists list_endpoints, and GET /api/callers / GET /api/repos/{id}/callers report the HTTP endpoints routed to a handler in routes_to, so a handler reached only over HTTP is not reported as unused.

Upgrade knot to 1.12.0. Updated the knot dependency from 1.11.12 to 1.12.0. Upstream adds an HTTP endpoint catalogue for Java/Kotlin (JAX-RS and Spring MVC handlers become http_endpoint entities linked to their handler by a ROUTES_TO edge) (1.12.0). Kotlin FQNs now carry their package (1.11.13); local JS/TS variables are no longer indexed as class members and this.m() walks the supertypes (1.11.14); calls inside one-line Groovy methods are attached to them (1.11.15); same-named Java/Kotlin types resolve through the caller's imports (1.11.16). Re-index Java, Kotlin, TypeScript/JavaScript and Groovy repositories to pick up the new entities and corrected edges.
POST /api/repos rejects a local path that does not exist with 400 instead of accepting it and failing in the worker. A local source must exist when it is registered.

entries.title: Upgrade knot to 1.11.12
entries.summary: Updated the knot dependency from 1.11.9 to 1.11.12.
highlights: Upgrade knot to 1.11.12. Updated the knot dependency from 1.11.9 to 1.11.12. Upstream, Kotlin, TypeScript and Groovy calls carry their argument count so overload disambiguation applies to them, while arity never constrains JavaScript (1.11.10); cross-repo calls no longer bind to a dependency's homonym when the receiver type is local, and the primary project identity is picked deterministically (1.11.11); calls on types outside the indexed repositories (String.valueOf, a third-party ModelMapper.map) no longer bind to unrelated same-named repository methods (1.11.12). No API changes required. Existing indexes keep the wrong edges until re-indexed.

entries.title: Upgrade knot to 1.11.9
entries.summary: Updated the knot dependency from 1.11.7 to 1.11.9.
highlights: Upgrade knot to 1.11.9. Updated the knot dependency from 1.11.7 to 1.11.9. Upstream, Rust self.method(), field-path (self.repo.save()) and call-chain receivers now produce CALLS edges (1.11.8), and overload disambiguation no longer crosses classes: calls bind to the exact-arity overload of the receiver's own type (or its nearest supertype), Java invocations carry their argument count, and arity alone no longer resolves a name-only homonym (1.11.9). No API changes required. Existing indexes keep the missing/wrong edges until re-indexed.
